title: Foundations, Culture and Compliance
thread: Not a hit-and-run: a health journey.
goal: Understand who we are, how the business works, and how to speak safely. Nothing else unlocks until the compliance gate is passed.
gate: Compliance Gate: 20 questions, pass mark 90%, and zero red-flag answers. Unlocks every later week.
lab: Spot and Fix: 6 real-world messages containing unsafe claims; rewrite each safely. AI-marked, 20 marks.

lessons.title: Welcome to Health & Wealth: who we are and how we care
outcomes: Tell the Health & Wealth story and explain what makes the company different
Explain our code and culture, including 'not a hit-and-run, but a health journey'
Describe how Sweety serves your customers on your behalf
Set a specific 90-day goal
video: Who we are: a young company with big ambitions, and why the Academy exists
Our code: we love and care for people
Not a hit-and-run but a health journey: customers are loved enough to receive after-sales care and support, even outside the scope of products
What that looks like in practice: check-ins, listening, encouragement, and referring people to a doctor when that is what they need
Your role as a brand ambassador: how every conversation grows the Health & Wealth name
Meet Sweety: customers chat with the assistant in 8 languages, and it carries your name
The 8-week map and your 90-day goal: what, how much, by when
lessons.assess: Orientation and culture quiz, 10 marks: single choice, 'which reply reflects the Health & Wealth way?' scenarios, and ordering.
lessons.practice: Goal worksheet plus 'My Health & Wealth promise': in your own words, how you will care for your customers. The coach checks specificity and sincerity.

lessons.title: How the business works
outcomes: Trace a customer order from first message to delivery or collection
Name the ways a distributor earns without quoting figures
Explain your role at each step
video: The customer journey: referral link, Sweety conversation, recommendation, payment, delivery or collection
What happens automatically and what you do personally
Income streams in plain terms: retail, referrals, team building
Why we never quote income figures in conversation
lessons.assess: Order-the-steps question plus 4 single-choice. 10 marks.

lessons.title: Speaking responsibly about health
outcomes: Use 'supports, maintains, helps' language and avoid 'cures, treats, prevents'
Never diagnose, and never suggest stopping or replacing medication
Recognise when a customer needs a doctor first
video: Why claims rules exist and who they protect
Words we use and words we never use
The medication rule: always keep taking what the doctor prescribed
When to say plainly and warmly: please see a doctor
Why we never ask a customer what 'illness' they have; we ask what they would like help with
lessons.assess: Rewrite-the-claim scenarios (2 x 2 marks), spot-the-violation (2), 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: 3 customer messages, reply safely. Marked against the red-flag list.

lessons.title: Honest income talk and privacy
outcomes: Talk about the opportunity without guarantees or inflated claims
Handle customer details and testimonials with consent
Use the follow-up opt-in correctly
video: Income claims: why 'many people start earning in their first month' is not safe wording
Honest alternatives that are still encouraging
Personal information: what you may keep, share and never share
Consent for messages, photos and testimonials (POPIA basics)
lessons.assess: Spot-the-violation (3 x 2 marks) plus 4 single-choice. 10 marks.

title: Product Knowledge I: Technology, Range and Honest Science
goal: Know the range, the price tiers and the honest answer to 'does it work?'.
lab: Product Fact Sprint: 15 timed questions on codes, tiers, usage and evidence answers. 20 marks.

lessons.title: What makes APLGO different
outcomes: Explain Acumullit SA technology in two plain sentences
Describe the lozenge format and why it matters to customers
Avoid over-claiming about absorption
video: Plant extracts, negative-ion infusion and the dissolvable lozenge
Why customers like it: nothing to swallow, no water needed
What we say and what we leave out (wording to be approved by compliance)
Using ONE benefit at a time instead of reciting every feature
lessons.assess: Single-choice, match-the-term, and 'which sentence is safe' scenarios. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: explain the technology to a curious customer in 30 seconds (voice or text).

lessons.title: The range at a glance
outcomes: Name all 19 products by code and by name
State each product's price tier
Group products by what they support
video: Standard R860: PWR Apricot, PWR Lemon, GTS, SLD, RLX, NRM, STP, GRW
Premium R1350: MLS, ALT, HRT, ICE, HPR, LFT
Elite R1850: BTY, BRN, HPY, AIR
Elite Special R1620: PFT
Memory aids and how the packaging colours help
lessons.assess: Matching (code to name to tier), 10 marks. Flash-card mode available for revision.

lessons.title: Using the products well
outcomes: Give correct usage guidance for each product (daily or as needed)
Explain the 3 to 6 month consistency message
Answer 'can I take more?' correctly
video: Dissolve one lozenge in the mouth; some products are taken daily and some as needed
Daily: BTY, HRT, PWR Apricot, PWR Lemon, MLS, NRM, GRW, ALT, HPR, AIR. As needed: GTS, PFT, HPY, BRN, SLD, STP, RLX, ICE, LFT
Consistency beats quantity: more is not better
Early effects versus full benefit over 3 to 6 months
A supplement complements a healthy lifestyle and never replaces diet, exercise or prescribed treatment
lessons.assess: Scenario replies (3 x 2 marks) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: respond to 'I want to take four a day so it works faster.'

lessons.title: The honest answer on science and safety
outcomes: Answer 'is it proven?' honestly
Explain what ingredient-level research does and does not show
Describe registration and quality statements only in approved wording
video: What exists: published research on individual ingredients such as ashwagandha and avocado
What does not exist: large-scale clinical trials on the finished products
Never say 'clinical studies prove this works'
Registration statements: use only the wording compliance approves
Myths and facts: the 10 workbook myths, corrected for accuracy
lessons.assess: Scenario replies (2 x 3 marks), 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: a sceptical customer asks for proof. Scored on honesty, warmth and a next step.

title: Product Knowledge II: Matching Products to Needs
goal: Learn the range by customer need, not by catalogue order.
gate: Level 1 Certified Associate exam: 40 questions (product matching, claims, usage), pass mark 80%, plus the Compliance Gate on record.
lab: Match-the-Need Lab: 10 customer cases, recommend the best fit and explain why in one mechanism. 30 marks.

lessons.title: Energy, stamina and performance
outcomes: Recommend between GTS, PWR Apricot, PWR Lemon, STP and BRN
Explain each in one benefit and two ingredients
video: GTS: strength, stamina and vitality (ginseng, ashwagandha, green tea)
PWR Apricot for women, PWR Lemon for men
STP: recovery after exertion
BRN: mental performance and focus
Choosing between them with one question
lessons.assess: Case matching (4 cases x 2 marks) and 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: two customer cases, recommend and explain.

lessons.title: Stress, mood and sleep
outcomes: Tell RLX, HPY and GTS apart
Use calm, non-clinical language for mood and anxiety topics
video: RLX: calm and restful sleep
HPY: mood, relaxation and stress management
Where GTS and BRN overlap on stress resilience
Language to avoid: 'treats anxiety', 'mood stabiliser' and similar
lessons.assess: Case matching (3 x 2) plus spot-the-claim (2) and 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: a stressed customer who sleeps badly.

lessons.title: Weight, appetite and blood sugar
outcomes: Explain PFT and NRM correctly
Handle blood-sugar conversations safely
video: PFT: appetite, metabolism and weight management with diet and exercise
NRM: supports blood-sugar metabolism within a healthy range
NRM never replaces diabetes medication; always the doctor first
Combining with GTS in programs
lessons.assess: Case matching (3 x 2), medication-safety scenario (2), 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: a customer on diabetes medication asks if NRM replaces it.

lessons.title: Joints, digestion and liver
outcomes: Recommend between SLD, STP, MLS, ICE and HPR
Explain the MLS and HPR pairing
video: SLD: joint comfort and flexibility (turmeric, ginger)
MLS: digestion and gut health; HPR: liver and pancreas, gentle detox
ICE: occasional heartburn, overeating and regularity
STP versus SLD: recovery versus ongoing joint comfort
lessons.assess: Case matching (4 x 2) and 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: stiff joints plus a sluggish stomach.

lessons.title: Heart, immunity, breathing, skin and ageing
outcomes: Recommend between HRT, GRW, ALT, AIR, BTY and LFT
Keep heart and ageing language compliant
video: HRT: normal circulatory function, alongside diet and exercise, never a substitute
GRW: immune system, hair, skin and nails
ALT and AIR: respiratory comfort and immune support
BTY: skin, scalp and hair vitality
LFT: cellular and antioxidant protection
lessons.assess: Case matching (4 x 2) and 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: a customer with several concerns; recommend a sensible combination and say why.

title: CLOSER Part 1: Discovery
thread: We love and care for people.
goal: Learn to listen first. Clarify, Label and Overview, in our care-first version of Alex Hormozi's CLOSER framework.
lab: Discovery Lab: three personas. Marked on Clarify, Label, Overview and compliance only. 40 marks.

lessons.title: CLOSER and the care-first spirit
outcomes: Name the six CLOSER steps
Explain why you lead the conversation
Explain why every message ends with something for the customer to answer
video: Origin of CLOSER (Hormozi) and why we use a caring, not pushy, version
Clarify, Label, Overview, Sell the vacation, Explain away concerns, Reinforce
You steer; the customer should never have to work out what happens next
Every reply ends with a question, invitation or clear next step
lessons.assess: Ordering and match questions, 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: watch two sample chats, find the CLOSER step in each message.

lessons.title: Clarify
outcomes: Open with one warm question
Ask one follow-up on duration and impact
Avoid interrogating
video: First question: what is going on, in their own words
The second question: how long, and how much is it affecting your day
One thing at a time, acknowledge before you ask
Language: describe symptoms and goals, never diagnoses
lessons.assess: Best-next-question scenarios (4 x 2) and 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: Clarify with a vague opening message ('hi, I'm tired all the time').

lessons.title: Label and Overview
outcomes: Name the customer's problem back in one genuine sentence
Ask what they have already tried
Always ask about chronic or prescription medication
Ask permission for helpful tips, once
video: The Label: specific, warm, checked with them
Why Label is the step that makes the rest feel like care
Overview: what have you tried, what happened
The medication question, framed with care
Follow-up opt-in: ask once, respect the answer
lessons.assess: Write-the-Label (2 x 3 marks), medication scenario (2), 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: Label and Overview with a customer on blood-pressure medication.

lessons.title: The recommendation gate and shortcuts
outcomes: Know when you may recommend a product
Handle customers who name a product, ask for the catalogue or ask for a person
video: A symptom name on its own is never enough to recommend
Discovery complete means you move straight to the recommendation
Customer names a product: go straight to quantity
Catalogue request: show the range, skip discovery
Asking for a human or a nearby distributor: hand over at once
lessons.assess: Route-the-message scenarios (5 x 2 marks). 10 marks.

title: CLOSER Part 2: Recommend, Overcome, Reinforce
thread: The sale is the start of the relationship.
goal: Turn understanding into a recommendation, handle concerns honestly, and complete the order with care.
gate: Level 2 Certified Advisor: two full CLOSER simulations scoring 75 or more with no red flags, plus a 30-question knowledge exam at 80%.
lab: Full CLOSER Simulation: complete conversation from greeting to confirmed order, marked on the 100-point scorecard.

lessons.title: Sell the vacation
outcomes: Bridge into a recommendation in one or two sentences
Recommend one to four products ethically
Write a product caption that sells the outcome
video: Selling the outcome in their life, not the ingredient list
The short bridge: name the products, no pitch yet
Recommending more than one product only when it genuinely helps
Standard versus Premium: mention honestly, never to pad the order
Anatomy of a caption: why this fits you, price, one or two ingredients, how to use and the 3 to 6 month note, one objection line, invitation to order
lessons.assess: Caption-critique (2 x 3 marks) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: write a caption under 900 characters for a given customer.

lessons.title: Explain away concerns
outcomes: Respond to the common concerns honestly
Acknowledge, answer, and ask
Never overclaim to win the sale
video: Will I feel results right away? Some do, full benefit builds over months
Is it safe and regulated? Approved wording only
Will more work faster? No, consistency matters
Can it replace my medication or diet? No
Price: value, tier choice, and not rushing
Optional enrichment: Hormozi's Acknowledge, Associate, Ask (content to be confirmed against source)
lessons.assess: Best-reply scenarios (4 x 2 marks) and 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: a price-sensitive customer and a sceptical customer.

lessons.title: Asking for the order and Reinforce
outcomes: Invite the order without pressure
Give a genuine reinforcement line
Ask how they would like to receive it before asking for details
video: Leading the close: 'how many boxes would you like?'
Reinforce: one short line confirming a good decision
Delivery or collection first, then only the details needed
Never use false urgency
lessons.assess: Scenario replies (3 x 2) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: close a confirmed customer.

lessons.title: The Wellness Program consultation
outcomes: Explain when to use the full consultation
Run the four-question intake
Describe the three-phase programs
video: Blood-sugar, joint and men's-wellness programs
Four quick questions: current state, impact, goal, readiness 1 to 10
The 12-week phases: starter pair, expansion, maintenance
Symptom-and-goal language only, never diseases
lessons.assess: Program matching (3 x 2) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: run the intake with a persona.

lessons.title: Orders, delivery and after-sale
outcomes: State delivery fees and collection options correctly
Answer payment-status questions honestly
Follow up well after the sale
video: Delivery is a flat R155 for every delivery, whatever the city. Collection from an office is R0
Collection offices: Johannesburg, Durban, Empangeni, Pietermaritzburg; weekdays 9 to 5, Saturday 9 to 1
Never claim a payment has been verified unless you can see confirmation
Following up within 24 hours and at the 3-month mark
After-sale care: the health journey continues, including support that goes beyond products
lessons.assess: Calculation questions (4 x 1), scenario (2 x 2), 2 single-choice. 10 marks.

title: Prospecting and Building a Customer Base
thread: Every distributor is a brand ambassador.
goal: Find people to help, communicate compliantly, and keep customers for the long term.
lab: Outreach Lab: write three outreach messages and hold one warm-contact roleplay. Marked on tone, compliance and call to action. 40 marks.

lessons.title: Your story and the resource library
outcomes: Tell a short personal story that is truthful
Find and use the right library item at the right moment
video: Structure of a story: before, turning point, now
Using the testimonial library: search by need, product and audience
Rules for sharing: consent on file, compliance-approved items only
Never invent or embellish a story
lessons.assess: Select-the-right-asset scenarios (4 x 2) and 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: draft your story; the coach flags unsafe claims.

lessons.title: Your list and warm market
outcomes: Build a list of 50 people
Approach with respect and consent
video: Who to include and how to categorise
The first message: curiosity, not a pitch
Respecting no
Privacy and consent when contacting people
lessons.assess: Scenario replies (3 x 2) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: first-message roleplay.

lessons.title: Content and social media
outcomes: Create compliant posts
Use your Sweety link to route customers to you
video: WhatsApp status, Facebook and TikTok basics
Library templates and how to adapt them safely
Calls to action that send people to your conversation
What never to post: cures, income promises, unconsented testimonials
Brand voice and brand assets: representing Health & Wealth consistently and with pride
lessons.assess: Spot-the-violation (3 x 2) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: write one post; compliance check.

lessons.title: Follow-up, reorders and referrals
outcomes: Plan follow-up around the 3 to 6 month cycle
Ask for referrals naturally
video: Check-ins: day 3, week 2, month 1, month 3
Using the tips opt-in properly
Reorders and loyalty offers
Referral asks that feel like service
Caring for customers outside the scope of products: a kind word, a check-in, a listening ear
lessons.assess: Scenario replies (3 x 2) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.

lessons.title: Resilience and your daily routine
outcomes: Handle rejection
Run a simple daily activity routine
video: Reframing a no
Daily method of operation: contacts, follow-ups, learning
Tracking activity in the Academy
Staying consistent when results are slow
lessons.assess: Reflection and 5 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: set your first weekly activity target.

title: Recruiting and Business Presentations
goal: Present the opportunity honestly and apply CLOSER to a business conversation.
lab: Business Conversation Lab: roleplay with a business prospect, marked on the business version of the scorecard. 40 marks.

lessons.title: Customers and business partners
outcomes: Tell the two audiences apart
Make a natural invitation
video: A customer wants a health outcome; a partner wants income and purpose
Questions that reveal which is which
Invitation lines that respect a no
Never mix the two pitches in one message
lessons.assess: Scenario replies (3 x 2) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: decide which conversation to start.

lessons.title: The business presentation
outcomes: Deliver a short, honest presentation
Adapt for one-to-one, three-way and group settings
video: Structure: problem, opportunity, support, next step
What to show and what not to promise
Using a three-way call with your upline
Handling questions you cannot answer
lessons.assess: Presentation outline critique (3 x 2) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: 3-minute presentation, scored.

lessons.title: Compensation plan mastery
outcomes: Explain how the compensation plan works accurately
Explain ranks and bonuses without inflating
video: Retail profit, team commissions and bonuses (detail to come from the official plan document)
Rank requirements and how to explain them
Honest framing of what is typical
Using the official income disclosure only
lessons.assess: Calculation and scenario questions, 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: explain the plan to a sceptical prospect.

lessons.title: CLOSER for the business conversation
outcomes: Apply Clarify to Reinforce to a prospect's financial situation
Handle the common business objections
video: Clarify what they want from extra income
Label it and Overview what they have tried
Sell the vacation: the life they want, not the compensation plan
Explain away: 'I'm not good at selling', 'I don't have time', 'I don't know enough about supplements', 'Is this a pyramid scheme?'
Reinforce and welcome them into the Academy
lessons.assess: Best-reply scenarios (4 x 2) and 2 single-choice. 10 marks.
lessons.practice: Practice: full business roleplay.

lessons.title: Ethical recruiting
outcomes: Recruit without pressure, guarantees or inventory loading
Know the legal and reputational risks
video: Why ethical recruiting protects your business
No guaranteed income, no pressure to buy stock
Fair treatment and honest disclosure
What to do when someone changes their mind
lessons.assess: Spot-the-violation (3 x 2) and 4 single-choice. 10 marks.

lab: Capstone: three marked simulations plus plan review.

outcomes: Onboard a new distributor using the Academy
Set up their first week
video: Welcome, goals and their first lesson
Their first five conversations
Staying in touch with daily check-ins
Sending them to Week 1 first

lessons.title: Coaching your team
outcomes: Use the leader dashboard
Hold a short coaching conversation
video: Who is stuck, who is active, who is ready
Coaching with questions, not instructions
Recognition that motivates
Using the best roleplay clips as examples

lessons.practice: Practice: coach a stuck team member.

lessons.title: Leadership, ranks and culture
outcomes: Describe what good leadership looks like here
Plan to reach the next rank
video: Leading by example
Culture of compliance and care: protecting the Health & Wealth way as the company grows
Events, recognition and training
Rank path and the habits behind it

outcomes: Write a realistic 90-day plan
Set weekly activity targets
video: Goals from Lesson 1.1, revisited
Activity targets: conversations, follow-ups, learning
Review rhythm with your upline
Submitting the plan for coach review
